newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil economy should open up more - cenbank exec.
newsitem.headline: Brazil economy should open up more - cenbank exec.

text.p: A study by Brazil's Central Bank Foreign Affairs director Gustavo Franco says the country's economic future should consider a greater trade opening, O Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper said on Tuesday.

According to Franco's study, which was sent to President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, the country's new economic growth model should contemplate a greater trade opening "substantially larger, maybe the double or the triple, of what we have today," the daily said.
"The trade opening, in the critics' minds, leads necessarily to a foreign exchange crisis or condemn us to a mediocer growth," the study says.
Franco's 45-page study attempts to bury the main arguments against Brazil's foreign exchange policy and the economy's opening up promoted by the ongoing stabilization plan, O Estado said.
